explanation: An ancient Phoenician city located on an island off the coast of present-day Lebanon. The book prophesies its destruction.
A divinely inspired prediction or message delivered through a prophet.
A Hebrew prophet and the author of the Book of Ezekiel in the Old Testament, who conveys God's messages and judgments.
King of Babylon who reigned from 605 BC to 562 BC. He is mentioned in the book of Ezekiel as God's instrument for destroying Tyre.
The act of completely tearing down or ruining something, which in this case refers to the city of Tyre.
The process of constructing again what has been destroyed. In Ezekiel 26 it is prophesied that Tyre will never be rebuilt after its destruction.
